SEOUL: South Korea's Fair Trade Commission said on Wednesday (Nov 11) that the regulator levied fines totalling 1.6 trillion won (US$1.2 billion) on 15 domestic brokerage firms and banks for colluding at government bond auctions for more than three years. The regulator said that from January 2020 to June 2023, the 15 primary dealers exchanged information by phone or the Telegram messaging app on their bidding yields one or two minutes before the deadlines in 150 government bond auctions. In 145 of those auctions, they directly agreed on bidding yields and volumes, the commission said. Such activities resulted in an artificial rise in South Korean bond yields, the FTC said. The FTC said it expects the penalty to foster effective competition in bond auctions and increase the efficiency of national fiscal management.

Source: Reuters/ec

BEIJING, Nov 11 : Oil prices rose on Wednesday after falling to two-month lows in the previous session, as the market swung between hopes for a de-escalation in the Iran war and concerns about ongoing attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Brent futures climbed 71 cents, or 0.78 per cent, to $92.20 a barrel by 0119 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 49 cents, or 0.57 per cent, to $86.53. New data showed that 37 ships were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz and surrounding waterways in October, the highest monthly total since the start of the war, according to the Washington Institute for Near East Policy. And 10 attacks have been recorded so far in November. Videos posted on social media on Sunday and verified by Reuters showed a Navig8 tanker on fire near the coast of Oman, one of three tankers hit on Sunday for using "unauthorised routes" through the strait, according to the Iranian state broadcaster.

Another tanker was struck northeast of Oman's Lima, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency said on Tuesday. Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said in a separate statement on Tuesday that two tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines on the "unauthorized route" in the strait. "Even in the event a deal is struck, an increase in flows through the waterway would still depend on mine clearance, insurance costs and whether or not shipowners would even be willing to take the risk," LSEG analysts said in a November 10 note. "Meanwhile, attacks have not slowed." In the previous session, oil prices initially fell by more than $3 a barrel after US officials downplayed the need for further military strikes against Iran, but then gained back some of those losses after an Iranian security official said no talks were taking place between the two sides. US crude oil stocks rose in the latest week, market sources said, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. Crude stocks rose by 9 million barrels in the week ended November 6, the sources said. In Russia, oil refining capacity has been reduced by about 30 per cent since late October following renewed Ukrainian drone attacks, industry sources said. Russian and Ukrainian officials met in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday for their first peace talks since February as US President Donald Trump's envoys launched a fresh push to end the war.

Source: Reuters

TOKYO, Nov 11 : Japanese manufacturers' sentiment rose to its strongest level in more than five years in November as booming semiconductor demand underpinned broad-based optimism, while the non-manufacturers' mood hit its highest in over eight years, a Reuters monthly poll showed. The Reuters Tankan sentiment index for manufacturers rose to plus-27 in November, the highest reading since August 2021, from plus-22 in October. The poll, a leading indicator of the Bank of Japan's quarterly Tankan business survey, was conducted from October 27 to November 6 and received responses from 214 of 508 firms. The indexes are calculated by subtracting the percentage of pessimistic responses from optimistic ones, with positive figures indicating net optimism. The improvement in manufacturers' confidence was led by the electronics sector, where sentiment jumped to plus-39 in November from plus-25.

"Semiconductor demand, particularly for memory, is very strong," a manager at an electronics machinery company said. Sentiment in the precision machinery sector, which includes some chip-related equipment makers, also improved to plus-42 from plus-38. "Orders from both domestic and international remain robust," said a manager at a precision machinery company. Another respondent at a machinery firm said that product shipments for the semiconductor market have reached an "unprecedented level". Oil refinery and ceramics rose to plus-25 from plus-14, while chemicals improved to plus-33 from plus-27. The non-manufacturers' index surged to plus-35 in November from plus-23 to reach a level not seen since June 2018. Sentiment in information and communications rose to plus-29 from plus-8 thanks to strong orders. Services and others rose strongly to plus-43 in November from plus-19. One manager said that "tight labour market conditions persist among companies, keeping demand for talent at a high level." Looking three months ahead, manufacturers expect sentiment to edge up to plus-28 in February, while non-manufacturers see confidence easing to plus-29. Rising prices and higher interest rates weighed on both sectors, the survey found, with some firms struggling to pass on increased costs to customers.

NEW YORK, Nov 10 : The US Securities and Exchange Commission said on Tuesday it completed distributions from a $40 million fund created from civil fines paid by Elon Musk and his electric vehicle company Tesla to resolve the regulator's first civil enforcement case against the world's richest person. In a filing in Manhattan federal court, the SEC asked a federal judge to close the Fair Fund, created after Musk settled the SEC case in 2018 charging him with securities fraud for posting on August 7, 2018, that he had "funding secured" to potentially take Tesla private. His posts on Twitter that day caused Tesla's shares and trading volume to spike, with the shares closing more than 6 per cent higher than when he began posting. They later fell after it became clear Musk had not lined up financing. Musk and Tesla each paid a $20 million civil fine, with sums designated for investor victims of the alleged fraud. Neither defendant admitted wrongdoing. Musk also agreed to let Tesla lawyers review some Twitter posts in advance, and give up his role as chairman.

The SEC said a claims administrator distributed $41.53 million, including interest and after deducting fees, to 3,350 eligible claimants. Those claimants received 51.7 per cent of their approved claims because their losses exceeded the Fair Fund's size. Another 3,046 claims were rejected. The SEC said the approximately $449,000 remaining in the Fair Fund will go to the US Treasury. "Distribution of the Fair Fund is now complete," the SEC said. The case is separate from the SEC case accusing Musk of waiting 11 days too long in March and April 2022 to disclose his early purchases of Twitter shares. Musk settled that case by having a trust in his name pay $1.5 million, also without admitting wrongdoing. A federal judge approved that settlement in July, while expressing "significant misgivings" about whether the SEC let Musk off too easily. Musk is a former adviser to Republican US President Donald Trump. He bought Twitter in 2022, renamed it X, and later folded the social media platform into his rocket and satellite company SpaceX.

WASHINGTON, Nov 10 : The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission has warned prediction market startup Kalshi of imminent charges in a probe into whether it properly notified the agency about dozens of new products, a person familiar with the matter said on Tuesday. The regulator's notification to the company suggests the charges could come soon, said the person who requested anonymity because the decision is not yet public. Kalshi in a statement said the CFTC's warning "is about a procedural error involving the submission of a handful of contracts, many of which weren't live." "We are already addressing the issue," the company added.

Kalshi has rapidly expanded its product offerings since securing a legal victory over the CFTC in 2024, allowing it to list diverse event-based derivatives. However, critics of prediction-market platforms such as Kalshi and peer Polymarket argue that the products resemble gambling and could encourage addictive behavior.  In recent months, Kalshi has pursued a broader strategy of competing with traditional exchange operators such as CME Group and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange by expanding beyond event contracts into a range of asset classes through perpetual futures. Perpetual futures, often called "perps," are derivative contracts with no expiry date, allowing traders to hold positions indefinitely without rolling them over. They can also involve high leverage, increasing both potential gains and losses.  The company raised $1 billion at a $40 billion valuation late last month, co-led by Sequoia and Wellington, underscoring the growing popularity of such markets and strong institutional interest. Politico reported about the imminent charges earlier in the day.

LONDON, Nov 10 : British horse racing's welfare board on Tuesday unveiled a five-year strategy that will use AI, wearable technology and lifetime tracking of horses to prevent injuries, reduce falls and improve horses' well-being away from the racetrack. The new strategy sets out 20 priorities to improve welfare and safety of thoroughbred horses throughout their lives, spanning areas including veterinary research, injury prevention, the training environment and aftercare and extending the scope of oversight from foaling through training to life after racing. Horse racing is Britain's second most-watched sport but concern for equine welfare remains its biggest reputational challenge, with falls, fatalities and the treatment of horses at key racing festivals like Cheltenham and Aintree under constant public scrutiny. Fatality rates in jumps racing were largely unchanged at 0.47 per cent in 2025 even after measures to improve the safety of fences like changing the colour of markings in 2022.

The British Horseracing Authority says it extended the scope of its reporting to cover more horses in 2021 and that it would take time for the safety improvements to take full effect. The rate of fallers dropped below 2 per cent on a five-year average for the first time in 2025, BHA data shows.  Work to improve safety and reduce fatalities is ongoing and a priority for the sport, Minette Batters, independent chair of the Horse Welfare Board, told reporters. "It's never going to be a case of accepting fatalities," she said. "It's what can we continue to do to make the sport safer that sits front and centre of everything we're doing."  Collecting more data on all aspects of a horse's life will enable trainers, vets and racecourse officials to spot issues like weakness or heart problems before they lead to on-racecourse injuries, racing experts said. This can start as early as birth by educating breeders on how antibiotic use in foals can impact soundness or in training by using heart monitors and wearable tech to detect equine illness or underperformance. "We're standing at the beginnings of a technology revolution in training of horses, in management of horses," said Fred Barrelet, veterinary surgeon and independent member of the Horse Welfare Board. "It's also becoming accepted and part of the young next generation of trainers and breeders' repertoire and armoury for managing their horses." The strategy also includes an ambition to track the full lifetime of all horses bred for racing in Britain through the Retraining of Racehorses programme.

Source: Reuters

MADRID, Nov 10 : Spain's government has demanded that TikTok suspend its operations in Spain until it eliminates child sexual abuse material, it said on Tuesday, after a media report documented 1,183 explicit posts on the platform with millions of views. Youth Minister Sira Rego, whose ministry cannot singlehandedly ban the platform in Spain, has appealed to prosecutors and the Data Protection Agency to take action against the social media company, according to a statement by the ministry. "Social media cannot be lawless territory," Rego said. The request comes months after Sanchez's government requested a probe into X, Meta and TikTok for allegedly spreading AI-generated child sexual abuse material, as European regulators intensify scrutiny of big tech over harmful and illegal content.

NEW YORK, Nov 10 : US electricity consumption will rise to record highs in 2026 and 2027 due to power-hungry AI data centers and electrification, the US Energy Information Administration said in its Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO) on Tuesday. The EIA projected that power demand will rise from a record 4,216 billion kilowatt-hours (kWh) in 2025 to 4,306 billion kWh in 2026 and 4,370 billion kWh in 2027. If correct, 2026 would be the third year in a row of record demand. Demand is surging largely due to data centers dedicated to artificial intelligence. Homes and businesses have also been relying more on electricity and less on fossil fuels for heat and transportation. The EIA forecast that power sales in 2026 will rise to 1,546 billion kWh for residential consumers, 1,557 billion kWh for commercial customers and 1,061 billion kWh for industrial customers.

The all-time highs stand at 1,519 billion kWh for residential consumers and 1,503 billion kWh for commercial customers in 2025 and 1,064 billion kWh for industrial customers in 2000. As renewable output rises, the EIA said the share of power generation from coal will slide from 17 per cent in 2025 to 15 per cent in 2026 and 2027, while the share of natural gas in 2026 will hold steady from 2025 at 40 per cent, then ease to 39 per cent in 2027. The percentage of renewable generation will rise from around 24 per cent in 2025 to 25 per cent in 2026 and 28 per cent in 2027, while nuclear power's share will hold at 18 per cent in 2026 and 2027, the same as in 2025, according to the outlook. The EIA projected that gas sales in 2026 would slide to 12.2 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) for residential consumers and 9.4 bcfd for commercial customers, but rise to 23.8 bcfd for industrial customers and 37.4 bcfd for power generation. Those figures compare with all-time highs of 14.3 bcfd in 1996 for residential consumers, 9.9 bcfd in 2025 for commercial customers, 23.8 bcfd in 1973 for industrial customers, and 36.8 bcfd in 2024 for power generation.

Source: Reuters

Nov 10 : Anthropic said on Tuesday it was bringing its Claude assistant to video conference platform Google Meet, as the company pushes to integrate AI deeper into everyday office work. Earlier in the day, Anthropic launched a roadshow for its highly anticipated US initial public offering, with plans to raise as much as $64.4 billion at a $1.02 trillion valuation. The offering will test investors' appetite for the AI boom and Anthropic's massive spending plans. Called Claude Meetings, the new feature will let users add Claude to video calls as a visible participant. Anthropic said Claude would be able to follow the conversation and turn discussions into work in real time, while also drafting plans, creating timelines and answering questions in the call's chat. The feature is designed to shift AI's role in meetings from simply recording or summarizing conversations to doing the work that follows from them while the discussion is still taking place, Anthropic said.

Nov 10 : IBM said on Tuesday that it was ending US visa and green card sponsorship for a majority of roles in IBM Consulting, which employs more than 150,000 people. The move comes amid tight scrutiny of foreign tech hiring by Donald Trump's administration. Last month, it suspended Microsoft, Adobe and several major outsourcers, including Cognizant, Infosys and Tata Consultancy Services, from the Permanent Labor Certification process — a key step toward green cards for foreign workers. IBM Consulting has used US high-skilled visa programs to address skill shortages, but participation has been declining for years, a company spokesperson told Reuters. It opted to end sponsorship for most such roles as skill availability and client needs have evolved, the spokesperson added.

WASHINGTON, Nov 10 : Alphabet's Google has agreed to additional privacy protections in the acquisition of employee data from defunct Spirit Airlines, a union representing employees said Tuesday. The agreement clears the way next week for approval of Google's $10 million deal to acquire Spirit data to train AI models. The union said it had won a more rigorous de-identification process than previously planned and added significant employee data will be excluded from the sale, including health and medical information. As part of Spirit's closure and asset liquidation, Google won an auction in August for data from emails, spreadsheets and calendars, as well as for marketing, productivity and operations. Spirit Airlines halted operations in May. A bankruptcy judge is now set to approve the deal next week.

The Association of Flight Attendants-CWA said the de-identified data will also be reviewed by an independent verification agent chosen in consultation with unions, and Google is prohibited from attempting to re-identify the data and is required to process it in a secure environment and treat it as confidential. A group of about 120 lawmakers raised concerns last month about the data sale. Last month, a privacy ombudsman recommended a US bankruptcy judge approve the deal after excluding passenger personal information from 97 million Spirit customers. The lawmakers, led by Senator Elizabeth Warren, a Massachusetts Democrat, and Representative Steven Horsford, a Nevada Democrat, said the sale would include 100 million emails, 500 million Microsoft Teams messages and other employee records. Spirit Airlines said it was pleased to have reached a resolution with labor unions as it continueed to maximize value for its creditors. "We are grateful for the collaboration of Google, the consumer privacy ombudsman, our labor unions, and other key stakeholders who are engaging with us constructively on this sale," a spokesperson said. Google, which did not immediately comment Tuesday, said last month it did not want to acquire personal information. "We are not looking to buy any personal information from Spirit. The information will either be completely excluded or will be de-identified by an independent third party before Google receives any data," Google said last month.
